info.title: Archive relay
info.description: HTTP over Door's service and World's query and named views (ADRs 0056, 0060, 0082), derived media and practice audio by content digest (ADRs 0069, 0089), document staging (ADR 0085), and exports (ADR 0089), for the operator and, on a relay with a circle, its members (ADR 0088). Every answer is JSON: {ok, archive, result} or {ok: false, error: {code, message}}, except a file route's success, which is the file's bytes, and a local probe's /health, which is liveness only (ADR 0114). Codes are stable; messages are not. The archive block names the archive, its specification, the relay's role and writes, the World projection versions it serves, the caller and their capacity, and the circle.

RefusalCode.description: Stable codes (ADR 0058, ADR 0060). Codes are only added; a client treats an unknown code by its HTTP status.

oneOf.description: Relay (403): A draft names an agent other than the caller's.
Door (503): Door could not read the archive's committed state. Nothing was written; the operator must look.
Relay (413): The body is larger than 1 MiB.
Relay (403): This relay runs in dry-run mode; it passes only dry runs to Door.
Door (500): Door's configuration, such as its Git or git-annex executable, is wrong or changed. Nothing was written.
Relay (422): The bytes or the declared type are audio or video; the relay stages and serves documents only (ADR 0085).
Relay (422): The bytes are not what their declared type says.
Relay (422): An Artifact carrying staged bytes is not described, in the same batch, by a document source claim of the type it was staged as.
Relay (422): The admission lists content the relay did not stage for this caller; other content admission stays with operator tools (ADRs 0056, 0085).
Relay (502): Door's service did not give a usable answer to a dry run.
Relay (503): Door's service could not be reached; nothing was sent to it.
Door (409): An expected head no longer matches the archive. Read the current heads, rebuild the proposal, and send it again.
Relay (502): The exporter failed or wrote no file.
Relay (404): World holds no revision an export renders or joins.
Relay (422): No exporter of that id and version is installed on the relay's host.
Relay (404): The feature bank holds no entry with this feature for this content.
Relay (404): The relay's configuration does not serve this feature, or no installed extractor declares it as an audio file (ADR 0089).
Relay (202): The feature is not made yet, and the bank has a scheduler: the relay has filed a bank request for it (ADR 0112). Ask again later; this is not a failure of the request.
Relay (403): The caller's tailnet login is not allowed.
Relay (403): The request's Origin is not listed.
Door (500): Bytes or committed evidence did not verify. Nothing was admitted; the operator must look.
Relay (500): The relay or Door failed unexpectedly. Door (500): Door failed unexpectedly. Report it.
Door (500): An operating-system read or write failed.
Relay (411): The request has no Content-Length.
Relay (403): Content is served only to the active operator's person and to circle members the recording or document is disclosed to (ADRs 0069, 0088, 0089).
Relay (404): The content is known but this derivative has not been made, or the relay has no derived-media root configured.
Relay (415): The declared media type is not a document type the relay stages.
Relay (404): No Artifact in World's selected generation has this content, or a destroy transition names it.
Relay (405): The route answers another method, named in Allow.
Relay (403): A read or a draft names something the caller's circle cannot read, whether or not it exists (ADR 0088).
Relay (404): No such route.
Door (500): The operation failed in a way that has no narrower code yet.
Relay (403): This route, request, or contract is the operator's (ADR 0088).
Door (503): Door cannot tell whether the write committed. Send the identical proposal again: a committed batch answers as a retry.
Relay (404): The requested projection version is not served; the archive block lists those that are.
Door (422): The proposal directory, manifest, or a draft cannot be read as a proposal. Fix the proposal.
Door (422): The proposal is well formed, but Door refuses it against this archive. Change the proposal.
Relay (400): The query is not valid SPARQL 1.1, or the engine could not evaluate it.
Relay (400): The query asks for something World does not answer, such as SERVICE.
Relay (504): The query ran past the relay's time limit and was stopped.
Relay (422): The answer would exceed the relay's row bound; nothing is returned, never a truncated answer.
Relay (416): The Range starts past the end of the derivative; Content-Range names its size.
Relay (502): The last render of these settings failed; the next request tries again.
Relay (422): No renderer of that id and version is installed on the relay's host.

Relay (400): The request is not a valid request for its route: its body, its Content-Length, or its fields. From Door: the relay sent Door an invalid request, which is a relay fault. Door (502): The service request itself is not a valid request. Fix the client.
Relay (404): The named stems entry is not in the bank, or is not the one the installed extractors give the recording.
Door (500): A program Door runs, such as Git or git-annex, failed.
Relay (415): The body is not application/json.
Relay (404): The view is named, but not at that version.
Relay (400): The view request, its subject, or a parameter breaks the view's rules.
Relay (404): World holds no record the subject names.
Relay (404): No view is named so (ADR 0082).
Relay (503): World's store cannot be read.

Archive.description: Present on every answer to an allowed caller.

role.description: Fixed in the relay's configuration. A client commits only where it is scratch, or live with writes commit (ADR 0088's amendment of ADR 0060).

caller.description: The person the caller's login is bound to, and whether they act as the operator or as a member of the circle (ADR 0088).

circle.description: Present on a relay configured with a circle: the destination's name and, when configured, the band's organisation.

SparqlResults.description: W3C SPARQL 1.1 Query Results JSON Format.

query.description: A SPARQL 1.1 SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT, or DESCRIBE query. World's data is in named graphs; the default graph is empty.

projection.description: The projection version the client was written for. Required, so a new version never changes an old client's answers.

rdf_format.description: The media type of a CONSTRUCT or DESCRIBE answer. SELECT and ASK answers are always SPARQL Results JSON.

snapshot.description: The archive commit the answer reflects.

data.description: SPARQL Results JSON for SELECT and ASK. For CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE, N-Triples or Turtle text, or expanded JSON-LD as a JSON array, as rdf_format asked.

Proposal.description: A Door proposal (ADR 0023, ADR 0028): the manifest, and each draft it names under records/<name>.json. Every draft's agent must be the caller's.

door.description: Door's own result, exactly as door/service.schema.json describes it.

oneOf.description: Door committed, but World did not refresh; queries answer from an earlier snapshot until a later refresh succeeds.

commit.description: The source commit the relay runs, or null when it cannot tell (ADR 0114).

build.description: How the relay was built: the Nix output's name, `export` (a `git archive` copy), `checkout` or `checkout-dirty`; null when unknown (ADR 0114).

ViewRequest.description: A named view, its version, its subject, and optional parameters; world/views.py checks the rest, failing closed.

snapshot.description: The archive commit the answer reflects.

parameters.description: Every parameter, defaults filled in.

answer.description: The view's answer; its version fixes its shape.

withheld.description: How many records were kept from the caller (ADR 0082).

content.description: The document's bytes, at most 64 MiB.

Staged.description: The row an admission manifest's contents needs, the canonical media type, and the Artifacts already carrying these bytes.

regions.description: Present when a configured feature has no whole entry but region entries (ADR 0112, a recording made under --songs): each region entry's file, by region. Its name stays in missing; fetch it from /media/{digest}/bank/{extractor}/{output}/{key}.

region.description: The region of the recording the entry was made over: [start, end) in samples at rate.

offset_seconds.description: Where the file starts on the recording: start / rate.

queued.description: Present when the bank has a scheduler (ADR 0112): the configured features not made, each asked for with a bank request, and the key its entry will have, which a practice request may name.

PracticeRequest.description: ADR 0089's practice request; check_practice_request in world/exports.py is the rule.

status.description: ready: the render exists; rendering: it is being made; queued: the stems it mixes are not made yet and the bank's scheduler has been asked for them (ADR 0112). Ask again while rendering or queued.

ExportRequest.description: ADR 0089's export request; check_request in world/exports.py is the rule.

LocalHealth.description: The answer to a GET /health from the relay's own machine that carries no tailnet identity and was not forwarded (no Tailscale-*, Origin, X-Forwarded-For or Forwarded header): liveness only, with no archive block (ADR 0114).

commit.description: The source commit the relay runs, or null when it cannot tell (ADR 0114).

build.description: How the relay was built: the Nix output's name, `export` (a `git archive` copy), `checkout` or `checkout-dirty`; null when unknown (ADR 0114).

tailnet.name: Tailscale-User-Login
tailnet.description: Set by tailscale serve from the caller's tailnet identity; the relay allows only configured logins and binds each to one agent.

get.summary: The waveform peaks (an audiowaveform binary file, version 2, 8-bit, every channel, about ten milliseconds a pixel) of an Artifact's content, by its digest
get.description: Derived media are regenerable, made by enrich/media.py into the relay's derived-media root (ADR 0069). Served only for a digest that is an Artifact's content in World's selected generation and that no destroy transition names, and only to the caller bound to the active operator's person or to a circle member the recording is disclosed to (ADRs 0088, 0089). One byte range is honoured; several ranges, another unit, or an unreadable Range header are ignored and the whole file is sent. If-Range is honoured with the entity tag.

parameters.name: digest
parameters.description: The content digest, as World projects it.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: One range of bytes, bytes=first-last, bytes=first-, or bytes=-suffix.

parameters.name: If-Range
parameters.description: The entity tag the range was taken from; any other value sends the whole file.

200.description: The whole waveform peaks (an audiowaveform binary file, version 2, 8-bit, every channel, about ten milliseconds a pixel).

ETag.description: Names the content digest and the method version, "sha256:<hex>/<kind>-<version>".

206.description: The range of the waveform peaks (an audiowaveform binary file, version 2, 8-bit, every channel, about ten milliseconds a pixel) asked for.

ETag.description: Names the content digest and the method version, "sha256:<hex>/<kind>-<version>".

400.description: request_malformed (the digest is not sha256:<64 lowercase hex>), or query_invalid.

422.description: query_too_many_rows, from World's media lookup under a very small row limit.

500.description: internal_error: World's answer or the derived-media root could not be read.

get.summary: Every named view and version World serves (ADR 0082)
get.description: From World's one registry, which the view route also dispatches through.

post.summary: Answer one named view from World's selected generation (ADR 0082)
post.description: The caller's person is the default person or judge. A member's view reads only their readable set (ADR 0088), states how many records were withheld, and may name nothing outside it (not_disclosed); the readable set, reach, and may_publish views are the operator's. Answers are cached per generation, request, and caller.

404.description: not_found, view_unknown, view_not_served, view_subject_not_found, or projection_not_served.

post.summary: Stage a document's bytes for admission (ADR 0085)
post.description: The operator only. Refuses audio and video, types not on ADR 0085's list, and bytes that are not what their type says. Staging admits nothing: the client then sends an admission through /door/admit whose contents rows are the ones answered here, with a document source claim describing each Artifact. Staged bytes not admitted within seven days are removed.

get.description: Served under the recording's gate: the operator, or a member the recording is disclosed to. With a scheduler (ADR 0112), each configured feature not made is asked for and listed under queued with the key its entry will have.

get.description: Answered only when the feature is configured and declared an audio file, the digest is an Artifact's content, and the caller may hear the recording; the relay never runs an extractor. When the feature is not made and the bank has a scheduler, the relay files a bank request for it and answers feature_queued (202) instead of feature_not_made (ADR 0112).

get.summary: One configured audio feature from the bank entry with this key, whole or over a region (ADR 0089, 0112)
get.description: The listing's features and regions name the key of the entry holding each file; a recording made under enrich backfill --songs has its stems as region entries, whose files start at the region's offset_seconds on the recording. Answered only when the feature is configured and declared an audio file, the digest is an Artifact's content, the caller may hear the recording, and the key is the whole entry's or a current region entry's; the relay never runs an extractor and asks for nothing here.

post.summary: Ask for a practice render of a mix of the recording's stems (ADR 0089)
post.description: Ready when the render exists; otherwise the relay begins it, one render at a time in the background with a renderer installed on its own host, and answers rendering, and the client asks again. Same gate as the stems. When the stems are not made, the bank has a scheduler, and the request names the key their entry will have (the bank listing's queued), the relay asks for them and answers queued; otherwise stems_not_made.
